title: Introduce Typology Entity
description: Introduce Typology as first-class entity: Kit owns typologies (not types/designs directly). Typology owns types and designs. Family stays at kit root for port compatibility. Type/Design keep families refs. Refactor Rust, GraphQL, schemas, SQL, all clients, fixtures, tests. No legacy.
summary:
Fixed the 12 CS1061/CS0117 build errors on KitDiff.Types/Designs/ShouldSerializeTypes/ShouldSerializeDesigns left over from the Typology refactor. KitDiff only exposes Typologies now, so: Kit.CreateDiff builds a TypologiesDiff (one TypologyModification per kit.Typologies entry, each carrying a nested TypesDiff/DesignsDiff) instead of top-level Types/Designs; Hashing.HashKitDiff hashes a single "typologies" field via new HashTypology/HashTypologyDiff/HashTypologiesDiff helpers (added in canonical alphabetical position between "tags" and "version"); KitInPlaceDiff.ApplyKitDiff routes through a new private ApplyTypologiesDiff that mutates kit.Typologies and re-flattens kit.Types/Designs, reusing the existing ApplyTypesDiff/ApplyDesignsDiff helpers. Also rewired ComposeDiff.ValidateKitDiff/RefSets, which walked JSON at diffObj["types"]/["designs"] (silently no-op once those keys stopped existing) — RefSets.FromKit now flattens type/design ids across kitObj["typologies"], and a new RunTypologiesIdCollection validates the typologies collection plus each modified typology's nested types/designs diffs (including heal-mode pruning, wired to actually patch the healed typology's diff object rather than just the outer collection). Updated Compose.Tests/cs/Tests.cs's Heal_Drops_Invalid_Design_Update to the new nested JSON shape.

Also fixed two unrelated but blocking issues discovered while trying to run `dotnet test`: Tests.cs's ResolveAssetsPath() still looked for "assets/fixtures" (renamed to compose/fixture at some point), and 24 call sites hardcoded the stale "stores/metabolism/wip/initialKit/kit.compose.json" path (renamed to "kit/dev/metabolism/wip/initialKit/kit.compose.json") — both were failing Tests's static constructor and cascading into ~53 unrelated test failures, making it impossible to verify anything.

Verified: `dotnet build` succeeds with 0 errors for both Compose.csproj and Compose.Tests.csproj. `dotnet test` now runs (was previously unable to build at all): 57/101 passing, including all 5 HashKitDiff_* unit tests. The remaining 44 failures are NOT caused by this fix — traced them to a separate, pre-existing, large-scale corruption of compose/fixture/*.compose.json (nearly every array field wrapped as {hash,items} instead of a plain array, incompatible with the C# List<T> model; some kit fixtures never migrated off flat types/designs) plus 3 tests needing a live GraphQL store server. Flagged as a background task suggestion (task_33a5c728) rather than fixed here since it needs a decision on the intended target schema and touches dozens of files unrelated to KitDiff.
